balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

revenueMix.title: Advertising vs other revenue
revenueMix.content:
Advertising revenue against everything else (data licensing, subscriptions, transactions).

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: other revenue is often contract-based and lumpy; one renewal can move it a lot.

What to watch:

  • Concentration of other revenue in a few counterparties
  • Advertising growth decelerating, which leads the cycle

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Alphabet Inc. Class A: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

segRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segRevenue.content:
Revenue by Google Search & other, YouTube ads, Google Network, Subscriptions/platforms/devices, Cloud and Other Bets.

For Alphabet: Search is still the profit engine; Cloud and Subscriptions are the diversifiers. Segments are shown as separate bars (read the sum as total revenue).

What to watch:

  • Search growth vs Cloud growth
  • Network shrinking as a share
  • Segment lines begin when first disclosed, so early periods are blank

segOI.title: Segment operating income
segOI.content:
Operating income of Google Services, Google Cloud and Other Bets.

For Alphabet: Services funds everything; Cloud turned profitable and now scales; Other Bets loses ~$2bn a quarter. Cloud OI for 2018-2020 is on the pre-2023 segment basis, so it is not strictly comparable.

What to watch:

  • Cloud margin trajectory
  • Other Bets losses vs Services profit
  • Basis break in Cloud OI at 2023

backlog.title: Backlog (remaining performance obligations)
backlog.content:
Contracted revenue not yet recognised, mostly Google Cloud.

For Alphabet: Backlog is the forward indicator for Cloud growth and AI-compute demand. From Q1 2026 the definition changed to include contracts of one year or less, so the step-up at Q1 2026 is partly definitional, not purely new demand.

What to watch:

  • Growth after the Q1 2026 definition change, not the jump itself
  • Backlog vs Cloud revenue conversion

adPricing.title: Paid clicks and CPC, impressions and CPM (YoY %)
adPricing.content:
Volume (paid clicks, impressions) and price (cost-per-click, cost-per-impression) growth for ads.

For Alphabet: Ad revenue growth splits into volume and price. Before 2019 paid-click metrics covered Google properties only; from 2019 they cover Search & other, so the series is not like-for-like across that break.

What to watch:

  • Falling CPC with rising clicks (AI Overviews mix, new surfaces)
  • Network impressions declining

tac.title: Traffic acquisition costs
tac.content:
Payments to distribution partners (browser and device defaults) and Network publishers.

For Alphabet: TAC is the main variable cost of Search and Network; rising TAC vs revenue pressures gross margin.

What to watch:

  • TAC as a share of ad revenue
  • Changes to default-search arrangements

headcount.title: Employees
headcount.content:
Period-end headcount.

For Alphabet: Revenue per employee shows operating leverage; headcount growth signals AI hiring against cost discipline.

What to watch:

  • Headcount growth vs revenue growth

cashInv.title: Cash and short-term investments
cashInv.content:
Cash & equivalents alongside short-term investments (marketable securities).

For Alphabet: Cash alone understates liquidity; the securities portfolio is the larger part of the net-cash position.

What to watch:

  • Drawdown from buybacks, dividends and AI capex
  • Debt issuance funding capex
